URL parsing and percent-unescape functions for HTTP and HTTPS strings.

# Purpose
This file implements URL parsing and percent-decoding helpers for `fd_url`. The [`fd_url_parse_cstr`](<#fd_url_parse_cstr>) function reads a URL from a character buffer and fills an `fd_url_t` structure with pointers and lengths for the main URL parts: `scheme`, `host`, `port`, and `tail`. It accepts only `http://` and `https://` schemes, rejects user information in the authority part, and reports parse errors through `opt_err`. It also checks the host length and returns `NULL` when the input does not match the supported format.

The file also defines [`fd_url_unescape`](<#fd_url_unescape>), which decodes percent-escaped text in place. It scans a buffer, converts hexadecimal escape sequences into bytes, and compacts the result into the same memory region. The helper [`fd_hex_unhex`](<#fd_hex_unhex>) converts one hexadecimal character into its numeric value and supports both lower-case and upper-case digits. Together, these functions provide basic URL handling for code that needs to parse and decode URL strings without using a larger external parser.
